newsitem.title: USA: GM to revamp Detroit's Renaissance Center.
newsitem.headline: GM to revamp Detroit's Renaissance Center.

text.p: General Motors Corp. said Tuesday it will spend hundreds of millions of dollars to renovate its new Renaissance Centre headquarters complex and make the fortress-like structure more inviting to pedestrians.

GM said the renovations, to be accomplished over the next five years, will include a five-story glass atrium overlooking the Detroit River and removal of two huge concrete berms at the front of the building that house heating and air conditioning equipment.

GM purchased the tubular glass complex, Detroit's most prominent downtown property, for $75 million about a year ago to serve as its global headquarters. The Renaissance Centre was built in the 1970s with backing from Ford Motor Co. at a cost of about $350 million.

The facility will eventually house 7,000 to 8,000 GM employees. The automaker is currently in the process of moving its six vehicle marketing divisions from cities throughout Michigan to the Renaissance Centre, a process that will be complete in late 1998.

Although GM did not disclose the total cost of the project, officials said one of the most expensive changes will be the removal of the concrete berms and relocation of the heating and air conditioning systems at a cost of $20 millionto $30 million. The structures now separate the building from Jefferson Avenue, the city's main downtown artery.

GM Vice Chairman Harry Pearce said the berms give the complex "the sense of a magnificent castle surrounded by a concrete moat. They reminded me of oversize tank traps that I'd see on European battlefields when doing research on military history."

Although he said there was not a direct business benefit from removing the berms, GM believed it was important to make the structure more inviting to pedestrians. The facility will include extensive public spaces, including a GM heritage museum and a riverfront promenade with shops and restaurants.
GM also said it plans to renovate the 73-story Westin hotel at the centre of the complex, one of the nation's tallest.

GM real estate director Matthew Cullen said the automaker in the next 60 to 90 days will choose a new hotel manager from a group that includes Westin Hotels & Resorts, Marriott International Inc., Hilton Hotels Corp., ITT Corp.'s ITT Sheraton, and Interstate Hotels Co.
The hotel management firm may be asked to contribute some of the capital costs of refurbishing the 1,392-room facility, Cullen said.
